questions.question: What type of assets do publicly listed Indian InvITs primarily own?
options: Operational infrastructure such as power transmission lines, highways, and pipelines
questions.explanation: Public InvITs in India hold operational national infrastructure assets like interstate power grids and toll expressways.

questions.question: What percentage of Net Distributable Cash Flows (NDCF) must an InvIT distribute under SEBI guidelines?
questions.explanation: SEBI InvIT Regulations mandate that at least 90% of NDCF must be distributed semi-annually or quarterly to unitholders.

questions.question: What happens to toll road assets after the contracted concession period (e.g. 25-30 years) with NHAI ends?
options: Ownership of the road reverts back to the government agency (NHAI)
The unitholders receive physical asphalt shares
questions.explanation: Under Concession Agreements, toll highways are built-operate-transfer (BOT) or toll-operate-transfer (TOT) assets where ownership reverts to the government after the concession term.

questions.question: What is the minimum lot size for trading public InvITs on the National Stock Exchange today?
questions.explanation: SEBI standardized the minimum trading lot size to 1 unit for publicly listed InvITs.

questions.question: How do InvIT returns predominantly behave compared to rapid tech stocks?
options: InvITs grow 100% every year like speculative startups
InvIT returns are predominantly driven by predictable cash yields and steady payouts rather than high capital appreciation
InvIT returns are completely tax-free under all conditions
questions.explanation: Because infrastructure assets amortize over their concession life, InvIT total returns are primarily driven by periodic cash distributions.
